responses.independent_answer: To record when bark was last harvested
responses.evidence: Paragraph 1: the trunk is marked with the final digit of the harvest year, helping workers identify when it was last stripped.
responses.relationship_or_option_eliminations: Amount removed is not recorded; species identification is not the stated purpose; the passage says the bark grows back.

responses.evidence: Paragraph 3: the second crop is generally unsuitable for quality stoppers; the desired structure is usually obtained from the third and later crops.
responses.relationship_or_option_eliminations: A newly planted tree has no crop; the first is irregular and unsuitable; the second is still generally unsuitable.

responses.evidence: Paragraph 2 requires at least nine years between harvests. The second harvest at 34 therefore permits a third no earlier than age 43.
responses.relationship_or_option_eliminations: 35 is only one year after the second harvest; 34 is the second harvest itself; 52 adds an extra nine-year interval.

responses.independent_answer: Repeated bark harvests require both careful technique and waiting.
responses.evidence: Paragraphs 1 and 3 describe careful cutting to preserve the living tree; paragraphs 2 and 3 describe the nine-year interval and crop sequence.
responses.relationship_or_option_eliminations: Trunk thickness alone is insufficient; first cork is unsuitable for quality stoppers; trees remain standing and bark regrows.

responses.independent_answer: Colour is floated and arranged on the bath.
responses.evidence: Paragraph 1: drops of colour are supported at the bath surface and guided with a comb or tool; paper is then laid onto the surface to pick up the pattern.
responses.relationship_or_option_eliminations: Placing a completed sheet in a book is a later use; removing gum is unstated; painting dried paper reverses the described sequence.

responses.independent_answer: To show that marbling could complement written pages
responses.evidence: Paragraph 2: marbled colours frame rather than replace the calligraphy in a manuscript album.
responses.relationship_or_option_eliminations: The text expressly rejects replacement; it does not say all ebru patterns were combed; the example does not date suminagashi.

responses.independent_answer: Regular parallel lines shaped in the floating colour
responses.evidence: Paragraph 2 links a comb to a regular design and mentions combed lines; regular lines in floating colour are therefore strongest evidence of combing.
responses.relationship_or_option_eliminations: Concentric ink rings are linked to suminagashi; a gum bath says nothing about whether a comb was used; speckles framing calligraphy also do not establish comb use.

responses.independent_answer: They can share a broad method without sharing a precise recipe.
responses.evidence: Paragraph 3: shared uses do not prove the same recipe, and 'marbled' identifies a broad method but not the comb, liquid, or colours used.
responses.relationship_or_option_eliminations: The bath may use gum or carrageenan; uses extend beyond covers; more than one cultural tradition is identified.

responses.independent_answer: A difference between stored pond water and the falling sea
responses.evidence: Paragraph 1: gates retain pond water while the outside sea falls, creating the height difference that drives the wheel.
responses.relationship_or_option_eliminations: Millstones are driven rather than pumping water; a constant river describes a different mill; waves do not strike the wheel directly.

responses.independent_answer: The outside sea must fall enough to give the stored water a useful height advantage.
responses.evidence: Paragraph 2: after filling, the mill waits for a useful difference between pond and sea levels.
responses.relationship_or_option_eliminations: The pond is already full, so another incoming tide is unnecessary; the wheel need not be covered by rising sea; releasing all water would consume the stored head.

responses.independent_answer: That tidal water management and familiar milling machinery operated together
responses.evidence: Paragraph 3: at Totton and Eling, the dam and gates manage supply while the wheel and stones grind; much machinery resembles other watermills.
responses.relationship_or_option_eliminations: Common machinery is explicitly noted; the dam manages water rather than only serving as a bridge; no claim is made about identical millstones at every site.

responses.independent_answer: The difference in water levels can grow before the miller releases pond water.
responses.evidence: Paragraph 1: closed gates retain water while the outside sea falls; release occurs after a head has developed.
responses.relationship_or_option_eliminations: A closed sluice does not imply a turning wheel or constant speed; it prevents immediate emptying; later refilling remains possible.

responses.evidence: Paragraph 2 says the White Caterthun has a great stone fort with evidence of vitrification.
responses.relationship_or_option_eliminations: Entailment: the statement restates the passage's observation about its stone fort.

responses.evidence: Paragraph 2 says Brown Caterthun earthworks had been maintained, burned and rebuilt over time.
responses.relationship_or_option_eliminations: Contradiction: rebuilding is expressly reported, contrary to abandonment without later rebuilding.

responses.evidence: Paragraph 3 says the Rahoy evidence does not identify the person who set the fire; paragraph 1 says the circumstances of a particular fire may remain uncertain.
responses.relationship_or_option_eliminations: Unresolved: attackers are possible but neither identified nor ruled out by the passage.

responses.evidence: Paragraph 3 says the cavities explain a physical route from burned timber to fused rock but do not identify who set the fire; the conclusion says human intention remains open.
responses.relationship_or_option_eliminations: Contradiction: the passage explicitly limits the cavities to evidence of process, not why the wall was burned.

responses.evidence: Paragraph 1 says a solid panel diverts much airflow around itself, while an open mesh lets more fog pass through.
responses.relationship_or_option_eliminations: Contradiction: the statement reverses the given comparison of airflow.

responses.evidence: Paragraph 2 lists three features examined: strand thickness, gaps between strands, and surface coating.
responses.relationship_or_option_eliminations: Entailment: all three listed features match the statement.

responses.evidence: Paragraph 3 discusses several meshes in series but says no measured annual yield for such a series is given.
responses.relationship_or_option_eliminations: Unresolved: the passage provides no basis for the exact three-screen doubling claim, and it does not rule it out.

responses.evidence: Paragraph 3 says a mesh cannot collect droplets that never reach it; paragraph 2 identifies the finer mesh as an improvement under particular conditions.
responses.relationship_or_option_eliminations: Entailment: the stated physical requirement applies to the improved mesh too.
